confirmed: Eight-mode programmable photonics; four-photon GHZ, two-photon entangled and single-photon probes assemble a three-bit phase output.
Main experimental dataset uses 99 uniformly spaced phases on [0,2pi) and at most 5,377 retained repetitions per phase.
Comparison of mutual information is at the same number of successfully collected events, not equal emitted photons or total acquisition wall time.

Controlled feed-forward operations are represented experimentally by collecting all relevant phase configurations and post-selecting/post-processing the data; a real-time feed-forward controller is not demonstrated.

Raw-probability information advantage decreases at larger repetition counts. After DAE probability denoising, the reported advantage remains throughout the investigated repetition range (main Fig. 4b).
A separate feed-forward neural network refines phase estimates; training is on simulated/theoretical noisy probabilities, and Methods report 4,000 epochs with ten samples per batch for this network.

Methods report source brightness about 14%, total chip input-output transmission about 50%, mean detector efficiency about 85%, and useful coincidence rates about 5MHz/50kHz/8Hz for one/two/four photons respectively. These are different component metrics and should not be collapsed into one measured end-to-end efficiency.

SI Note 2D supplies a simplified balanced phase-independent efficiency model: NQ=4/eta^4+2/eta^2+1/eta, NC=7/eta. Mutual information per phase-interrogating photon remains advantageous only above about eta=83% in that model. The authors explicitly require individual stage-success probabilities for a complete loss analysis.

SI Note 2E adds posterior-variance comparisons at equal retained detected-event budgets; mutual information alone is not a SQL precision certificate. Four representative phase posteriors are displayed, and the SI uses a 100-phase wording there while main acquisition and SI2B use 99; do not combine those as a verified uniform full-dataset precision claim.

required_pdf_corrections.instruction: Qualify repetition-dependent weakening as raw-data behavior and preserve the DAE-corrected advantage over the investigated repetition range.

required_pdf_corrections.suggested_short_text: 조건부 위상 설정별로 얻은 측정 자료를 후선택·후처리로 결합해 inverse QFT를 구현하고, 최종 세 비트로 위상을 읽었다.
같은 성공 검출 사건 수에서 고전 단일광자 간섭계보다 많은 위상 정보를 얻었다. 본문·보충자료·심사 기록은 공개되며, 원 데이터는 저자 요청으로 제공된다.
원시 확률의 이점은 반복 증가 시 약해졌으나 DAE 보정 뒤 조사 구간에서 유지됐다. 손실과 취득시간을 포함한 처리량은 별도 비용이다.

required_pdf_corrections.instruction: Record the SI balanced-loss model and approximate 83% threshold, distinguishing it from an experimentally measured efficiency or whole-sensor wall-clock advantage. State the post-selected feed-forward implementation and simulated NN training.

references.title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithm for Differential Equations: Application to Simulating a Biomolecular System
references.aps: M. Bagherimehrab, D. Farooqi, G. K. Brennen, B. C. Sanders, and A. Aspuru-Guzik, End-to-end quantum algorithm for differential equations: Application to simulating a biomolecular system, arXiv:2611.26582v1 (2026).
references.read_scope: Abstract/edition record; full sections3.1,3.4,3.5,4; relevant initial-state and preprocessing passages in2.2/3.2. Selected operator/preconditioning context; no full61-page or appendix-proof audit claimed.
conditions: Linearized Poisson-Boltzmann continuum electrostatics, not electronic Schrodinger wavefunction. Classical coordinates, partial charges and atom-ball cavity specify the dielectric/ionic model.

Electrostatic free energy is a charge-weighted average of neighboring grid potentials; solvation free energy is a difference of electrostatic free energies in two environments, not a full grid-vector output.
Polylogarithmic classical preprocessing in grid size/inverse accuracy is for fixed atom count.
Amplitude estimation gives the best overall quasilinear inverse-accuracy dependence; simpler Hadamard-test circuits have quadratically many repetitions.
Figure11 compares separately normalized quantum gate/classical full-vector multigrid arithmetic growth atN0=250; atom count/constants excluded; no conversion to physical runtime.
Grid discretization and algorithmic property error are distinct; no concrete molecular FTphysical-resource or QPU runtime demonstration.

Initial atom charge supports are assumed disjoint after sufficient grid refinement; atom-index preparation has explicit Theta(Natm) gate and Theta(Natm log Natm) classical costs before the fixed-atom scaling analysis.

references.title: Scaling classical hardware for accurate real-time quantum error correction
references.read_scope: All 13 pages: main text, Methods, Extended Data Figures 1–4 and Extended Data Table 1. Source Figure 1 (p2) and routed-build table (p10) rendered and opened. Zenodo official metadata, README, MANIFEST, selected d19 build README and RTL cosimulation record, code archive license and build manifest read statically.

findings.surface: At d=19, compact single VP1802 routed build uses 423.7MHz/400 cycles per round =0.944us throughput time, while decision latency is 8628 clocks=20.36us from RTL cosimulation. Strong throughput is not submicrosecond feedback latency.
findings.surface_error_comparison: 240-fold lower logical error per round than union-find at d=19/SI1000 physical error p=0.15%; nearly10x lower than MWPM. Union-find is a software implementation of the prior Helios decoder for error-rate comparison. Not a measured240x QPU speedup or universal decoder ranking.
findings.gross: [[144,12,12]] Gross code, uniform circuit-level depolarizing p=.1%; widest C128 routed build on two VP1802s gives0.331us/round,8.02us cosim latency;16fold lower per-logical-qubit error than real-time int4 X/Z-Relay-BP-1 configuration. Offline joint-basis floating-point Relay is different.
findings.execution: Paper and official dataset document synthesis/place-and-route reports, signing, generated RTL and cosimulation. No live-QPU closed-loop test or board-measured runtime was located. Use FPGA design/place-and-route/RTL evaluation, not measured physical hardware execution.
findings.power: Switching-activity/report_power estimates, not wall-power measurements. 7nm ASIC is ASAP7/OpenROAD predictive estimate. Chip-to-chip latency uses RTL simulation/link model.

references.title: Efficient Classical Algorithms for Ground Energy Estimation of Fermions with Conjugate-Pair Orbital Interactions
references.aps: Z. Yang, Y. Zhang, Y. Su, Xinzhao Wang, Xiaoyang Wang, and T. Li, Efficient classical algorithms for ground energy estimation of fermions with conjugate-pair orbital interactions, arXiv:2611.26382v1 (2026).
references.read_scope: Abstract/version, introduction/results subsection1.1 including Theorem1.1/algorithm roadmap and concurrent-work relationship; section2 definitions/model, especially2.3. Proof details and full41pages not audited; no algorithm rerun.
conditions: Conjugate hopping and conjugate-paired attractive interaction channels; not arbitrary molecular Coulomb Hamiltonians.
Ground-energy target over the full two-component Fock space, not an arbitrary prescribed particle-number sector.
Rational inputs; additive total-energy error epsilon with probability at least3/4.
Bit complexity polynomial in n,s,strength bound lambda,inverse epsilon,inputbitlength b; do not call polynomial in bitlength alone.
No physical spectral gap or weak-coupling assumption. No empirical large-lattice/QPU/industrial speed benchmark claimed.

references.technical_version: arXiv:2601.18164v3, 10 November 2026, 61 pages; public publisher DOI page and abstract checked separately, without claiming byte-identical accepted text.

confirmed: C-SWAP information selection, measurement-result feed-forward and time-shared parameters give a sequence-length-independent parameter count and per-step effective circuit depth; total sequential execution cost still grows with sequence length.

The reported 46.2–99.7% parameter reduction is a statevector-model comparison. WDBC includes same-protocol trained MLPs, while the extreme MNIST comparison uses a CNN result from separate literature; it is not a common matched-budget hardware comparison.
Hardware sequential inference is limited to one MNIST sample per each of two backends, not a hardware test-set accuracy benchmark.

ArXiv v3 Section 3.5 records one complete eight-step QESEM inference as 33 completed batch jobs, 4,301 seconds reported QPU usage (about1.2h), and about one week of wall-clock time including queue, mitigation and post-processing. These are author-reported historical operating conditions, not a general hardware runtime forecast.
